subject: Literature
subcategory: Classic Novels That Changed the World
title: Native Son and American Racism
description: A quick win: understand Native Son and American Racism.

hook.text: Richard Wright wanted white America to understand what racism felt like from inside a Black man's mind.

buildup.text: Native Son followed Bigger Thomas, a young Black man trapped by poverty and fear in 1930s Chicago.

discovery.text: Published in 1940, it became the first bestselling novel by a Black author through the Book-of-the-Month Club.

twist.text: Critics were shocked because Wright refused to make Bigger sympathetic or morally clean.

climax.text: The novel forced America to see racism not as a Southern problem but as a national systemic failure.

punchline.text: Wright made America look at what it had created.

quiz.question: What made Native Son groundbreaking?
options: It was the first novel published in America
It was the first bestselling novel by a Black author via the Book-of-the-Month Club
It was written entirely in poetry
